title: Web Interview Prep
body:
**Which machine does this actually happen on?** Every note below is built around that one
question, as a table pairing an everyday analogy with the technical term it stands for. The
interview-relevant skill is pointing at a piece of logic and saying which side of the
browser and server split it runs on, and what would break if it ran on the other side. The
recurring interview questions are that question in another form: [[CORS]], `HttpOnly`,
[[Client-Side Rendering]] against [[Server-Side Rendering]], and build time against runtime.

## Topics

- [[HTTP Requests]]: the lifecycle of one request. The JS that builds it, the methods and URLs and
  status codes on the wire, HTTPS, IP addresses, and the response that repaints the screen.
- [[REST APIs]]: the restaurant and menu model of a client-server contract. Endpoints, resources,
  auth, rate limits, pagination, versioning, webhooks.
- [[Cookies and Browser Storage]]: the wristband model. `Set-Cookie`, cookie flags, same-origin
  policy, CORS, localStorage against sessionStorage.
- [[Modern JavaScript Concepts]]: the DOM as a stage set. Reflow against repaint, the virtual DOM,
  debugging, and which work happens at build time and which at runtime.
- [[Server-Side Technology]]: front-of-house against back-of-house. The frontend and backend split,
  Rails MVC, and SQL storage concepts.

## Core Facts to Know

- The client chooses the method, URL, and body. The server only chooses how to respond.
- [[CORS]] and the [[Same-Origin Policy]] are enforced by the browser, never by the server.
- Cookies are attached automatically by the browser. [[localStorage]] never is.
- `HttpOnly` protects against [[XSS]]. `SameSite` protects against [[CSRF]].
- Bundling, minification, tree shaking, and transpiling all happen at build time, never in the
  user's browser.
- Anything on the frontend can be read and modified by the user, so trust has to live on the
  backend.

## Related courses

- COMP 3612, [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]]: [[HTTP]], [[DNS]], [[Cookies]], [[CORS]], [[DOM]],
  [[Fetch]], [[Asynchronous JS]], [[Express]], [[Node.js]].
